claim: Affine group schemes are represented by commutative Hopf algebras; coproduct, counit and antipode induce multiplication, identity and inverse on points.
hypotheses: Commutative base ring; affine group scheme.
verification: Milne2022 Definition 3.3 and adjacent Hopf algebra construction; Conrad2014 Definition 3.1.1 for reductive scheme scope.
limitations: This verifies the added definition, not construction or classification of every Chevalley scheme.

claim: A finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra module has an admissible integral lattice; admissible lattices decompose into weight components.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional module over a complex semisimple Lie algebra, fixed Chevalley basis.
verification: Ree1964 Definition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6; additionally read Kostant1966 Corollary 1 to Theorem 1 and its proof.
limitations: No Lean formalization of representation theory; lattice dependence and basis choices are retained.

claim: Root divided powers generate an integral form of the universal enveloping algebra; ordered negative divided powers, Cartan binomials and positive divided powers form an integral basis.
hypotheses: Complex semisimple Lie algebra with integral Chevalley basis.
verification: full Kostant1966 Groups Over Z, especially Theorem 1, proof §§2.5–2.6 and Corollary 1.
limitations: The integral enveloping-algebra theorem does not itself prove the modern group-scheme equivalence.

claim: The universal (simply connected) Chevalley group over a field has the stated Steinberg presentation after imposing multiplicativity of h.
hypotheses: Indecomposable root system; arbitrary field; relations A,B,C for rank at least two; B replaced by B′ for rank one.
verification: Steinberg2016 Chapter 6, Theorem 8(b), its setup and rank-one relation B′; earlier universal/simply-connected convention read.
limitations: Original Steinberg1962 full text was not located; no original theorem number inferred. Reducible root systems use componentwise extension, not literal Theorem 8(b).

claim: Columns of invertible matrices over a commutative ring are unimodular.
hypotheses: Square invertible matrix over a commutative unital ring.
verification: the corresponding row of the inverse pairs with the column to give 1.
limitations: Does not imply every unimodular column completes to an invertible matrix.

claim: Characteristic-free highest-weight orbit equations impose necessary constraints on columns over arbitrary rings.
hypotheses: Integral representation and polynomial identities vanishing on the group scheme; field orbit sufficiency requires algebraic closure and a nonzero point.
verification: Lichtenstein1982 is cited; its full characteristic and scheme-level scope has no independently verified locator in this register.
limitations: The phrase characteristic free alone does not prove scheme-level identities or sufficiency over arbitrary rings. No blanket source-verified status assigned.

claim: Reduction has kernel the principal congruence subgroup and yields an exact sequence ending in its image; full congruence subgroup is the inverse image of the quotient group centre.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring R, ideal I, fixed affine group scheme G.
verification: homomorphism/kernel definitions and group first isomorphism argument.
limitations: Reduction onto all G(R/I) is not asserted; central quotients and relative K1 require separately stated normality.

claim: The ring double is the pullback R×_(R/I)R; its projections split by the diagonal and have kernels (0,I),(I,0).
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring R and ideal I.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.mem_ringDouble_iff, double_square_commutes, double_projections_split, double_lift_projections, double_lift_unique, double_first_kernel, double_second_kernel and double_semidirect_product in checks/lean/Vavilov1991/RingDouble.lean. Componentwise ring operations give the compatible-pair universal map; semidirect coordinates give multiplication (ab,ad+cb+cd).
limitations: The first seven declarations concern the commutative ring double; the coordinate multiplication is valid over an associative unital ring. Neither preservation by a Chevalley functor nor elementary-group exactness is formalized.

claim: For the split projection of the double, the elementary kernel is its relative elementary subgroup; projection to the other factor identifies it with E(R,I). The elementary reduction square commutes, but its bottom row need not be exact.
hypotheses: Fixed Chevalley root group functor over commutative rings; ideal I; relative elementary subgroup defined by normal closure.
verification: Stepanov2014 §1.12 splitting principle; checked elementary argument: write split generator xα(a,b)=xα(a,a)xα(0,b−a), so kernel is the normal closure of the second factors. Under π2 these give level-I generators and conjugates; inverse identification follows their embedding in the kernel group of the represented pullback.
limitations: Representability gives G(D)=G(R)×_(G(R/I))G(R), not a general claim that elementary functors preserve arbitrary pullbacks. Normality transfer assumes absolute normality for every ring in question.

claim: Relative elementary groups are generated by conjugated root generators; long-root generation requires a separate G2 argument.
hypotheses: Reduced irreducible root system of rank at least two; commutative ring and ideal.
verification: The displayed non-G₂ rank-two Chevalley factorization has been checked algebraically. The original author’s assertion alone does not verify the remaining G₂ case.
limitations: Own-school source is not counted as independent source verification. Uniform G2 long-root generation is not certified by this selection; displayed argument explicitly only gives it when 2I=I.

claim: Basic representations are minuscule representations or the short-root representation; their nonzero weight spaces have multiplicity one.
hypotheses: Nontrivial irreducible finite-dimensional representation of a complex simple Lie algebra; Weyl group transitive on nonzero weights.
verification: Multiplicity-one deduction checked: Weyl invariance of weight multiplicities transports the one-dimensional highest-weight space. Complete classification and the asserted reflection criterion were not independently source-verified in this selection.
limitations: No certification of the full classification table or zero-weight multiplicity formula from this argument alone.

claim: Gsc(A_l)=SL_(l+1); Gad=PGL_(l+1); E consists of elementary transvections; root e_i-e_j adds xi v_j to v_i.
hypotheses: Commutative R; l≥1.
verification: Matrix-unit multiplication verifies the root action. Ree1957 and Hee1984 are cited for the scheme identifications; an independently checked proof locator is not recorded.
limitations: Matrix action verified; integral scheme identification requires an independently read locator.

claim: SL_n→PGL_n need not be surjective on R-points; its target is not generally SL_n modulo scalar matrices.
hypotheses: General commutative R.
verification: Counterexample over R=real numbers, n=2: projective class diag(-1,1) cannot be scaled to determinant one, since scaling multiplies determinant by a square.
limitations: Counterexample proves warning, not full cohomological description.

claim: SL_n/E_n defines unstable SK1 as a quotient group for n≥3; rank-one cosets may not form a group.
hypotheses: n≥3 and commutative R; exception n=2.
verification: Suslin–Taddei elementary normality supplies the quotient-group assertion for n≥3; the matrix generators agree by definition.
limitations: Full group normality is source-based, not formalized in Lean.

claim: Natural A_l weight diagram is a chain with labels alpha_i=e_i-e_(i+1).
hypotheses: Displayed compressed diagram, l=8–12 test instances.
verification: checks/sage/classical_diagrams.py compares actual vertex and complete induced edge literals with independent Sage root data.
limitations: Finite displayed instances; root description gives the symbolic extension, no arbitrary-rank formalization.

claim: Split odd quadratic form has maximal Witt index l; Spin and SO give simply connected/adjoint type B_l models.
hypotheses: Quadratic form x0²+sum xi x_-i; displayed bilinear equations assume 2 invertible.
verification: The displayed hyperbolic pairs exhibit the Witt index. The integral Spin/SO identification has no independently checked proof locator in this register.
limitations: Odd orthogonal group scheme in characteristic two requires its correct integral definition; determinant/polar-form equations below have 2-unit scope.

claim: Odd orthogonal Gram, inverse-entry identities, determinant condition, and necessary column norm zero or one.
hypotheses: 2 invertible; indices 1,…,l,0,-l,…,-1.
verification: a^-1=F^-1 a^t F proves entry equations; quadratic norm of a column follows a^tFa=F. checks/sage/classical_forms.py confirms ranks2–5 exactly.
limitations: Column norm is necessary, not asserted sufficient to extend a vector to an orthogonal matrix.

claim: Polar form is symmetric, nondegenerate and identifies V with its dual; O equals its isometry group.
hypotheses: 2 invertible in odd dimension; even hyperbolic Gram invertible over any R.
verification: F determinant is ±2 in odd rank; even skew-diagonal determinant is ±1; inverse-Gram algebra gives the dual isomorphism.
limitations: Cannot drop 2-unit assumption in odd dimension.

claim: Displayed long/short root matrices preserve Q, have determinant 1, form additive root subgroups and have the stated coordinate actions.
hypotheses: Commutative R; long i≠±j; short i≠0.
verification: checks/sage/classical_forms.py verifies the integral polynomial identities at ranks 2–5. Direct multiplication in the affected two or three coordinates proves additivity and the stated actions.
limitations: Finite Sage instances and the embedded coordinate argument do not identify the entire group scheme.

claim: Spin(K)=Epin(K); EO(K) is kernel of spinor norm and outside small dimensions equals Omega; KO differs from spinorial K1.
hypotheses: Field K; split quadratic space; 2-unit convention in surrounding matrix exposition; low-dimension exceptions unspecified.
verification: Bass1974, Bak1981 and Stein1978 are cited in the text; exact field hypotheses and low-dimensional exceptions are not verified here.
limitations: The unspecified small-dimensional exceptions prevent certification of the complete prose assertion.

claim: B_l natural weights form labelled chain, including zero; root coordinate additions agree with matrices.
hypotheses: Displayed compressed instances.
verification: checks/sage/classical_diagrams.py independently verifies vertices/edges; checks/sage/classical_forms.py verifies displayed action matrices.
limitations: No group-scheme identification from graph checks.

claim: Alternating form is perfect, Sp is its matrix stabilizer, Gsc type C_l and Gad=PSp.
hypotheses: Commutative R, l≥1.
verification: The alternating Gram matrix has determinant one and inverse −F; inverse-entry identities follow by multiplication. Integral Chevalley identification needs a separate proof locator.
limitations: Linear algebra verified; scheme classification not certified by finite matrices.

claim: C_l roots, long/short elementary matrices and coordinate actions are as displayed; root subgroups additive.
hypotheses: Opposite indices for long roots; i≠±j short roots.
verification: checks/sage/classical_forms.py ZZ polynomial preservation/determinant/inverse checks ranks2–5; direct matrix-unit multiplication proves additivity for all embedded patterns.
limitations: Sage does not prove elementary-subgroup normality.

claim: KSp_1=Sp_(2l)/Ep_(2l) is a quotient group.
hypotheses: Requires l≥2 over arbitrary commutative R.
verification: For l≥2, symplectic elementary normality follows from the Suslin–Taddei theorem cited in the text. For l=1 the model is SL₂/E₂, where normality cannot be assumed.
limitations: The rank restriction is explicit; the full normality theorem is source-based.

claim: Natural C_l diagram is labelled chain, terminal root 2e_l.
hypotheses: Displayed instances.
verification: checks/sage/classical_diagrams.py independent complete vertex/edge comparison.
limitations: Finite displayed instances, not all-rank formal theorem.

claim: Hyperbolic Q has maximal Witt index; Spin/SO/PSO are corresponding forms; intermediate lattices count one for odd l, three for even l.
hypotheses: D_l irreducible l≥4; SO matrix description 2 invertible.
verification: The intermediate-lattice count follows from P/Q≅Z/4 for odd l and (Z/2)² for even l. Conrad2014, Definition C.2.10 and Theorem C.2.11, supply the integral connected-orthogonal definition.
limitations: The complete root-datum identification and low-rank coincidences are not certified by the lattice count alone.

claim: Even orthogonal inverse entries, isotropic columns, long root matrices and coordinate actions.
hypotheses: 2 invertible for equivalence of determinant/polar-form description with SO; root matrices themselves integral.
verification: a^-1=f a^t f; column Q=0 via diagonal Gram entry; checks/sage/classical_forms.py preservation and determinant checks ranks2–5.
limitations: The inverse/column equations alone do not suffice in characteristic two.

claim: D_l diagram has two incomparable middle weights and specified root labels.
hypotheses: Displayed compressed instances.
verification: checks/sage/classical_diagrams.py independent complete induced edge check.
limitations: Claim concerns actual diagram, no assertion about every possible coordinate ordering.

claim: Alternation of the five given monomials defines the Dickson three-form; corrected Q has negative x0².
hypotheses: Commutative R; alternating form defined integrally.
verification: checks/sage/g2_forms.py verifies all 343 basis triples against split Zorn multiplication and diagnoses the printed quadratic-form error by exact tangent-space calculations.
limitations: Rational tangent diagnostic alone does not prove group-scheme identification.

claim: Split Zorn multiplication has unit, norm ab+u·v, trace a+b, and multiplicative norm.
hypotheses: Every commutative R; displayed signs fixed.
verification: checks/sage/g2_forms.py exact integral polynomial norm-composition identity; unit/trace by direct substitution. Conrad2015 ExampleB.2 supplies split model.
limitations: Composition identity is algebraic; classification of automorphisms uses separate theorem.

claim: Aut(split octonion algebra) is split group scheme G2 over Z, hence equality on R-points.
hypotheses: Every commutative R.
verification: Conrad2015, Theorem B.14 and Lemma B.13, pp. 58–59; Asok2019, Theorem 2.2.1. These primary-source statements supply the group-scheme identification.
limitations: Source theorem, not Lean/Sage scheme proof.

claim: When two is invertible, Q and F determine octonion multiplication and Isom(Q,F)=G2.
hypotheses: 2 invertible; trace-zero complement V.
verification: Trace decomposition R1⊕V; XY=−B(X,Y)/2·1+X×Y. Perfect B uniquely recovers X×Y from F; isometries extend fixing1. Converse norm/trace preservation from octonion automorphisms. checks/sage/g2_forms.py checks coefficient identities.
limitations: Uses the established octonion automorphism theorem; no claim in characteristic two for the seven-dimensional tensor description.

claim: The displayed signed short-root operator preserves Q and the Dickson form, extends to an integral Zorn automorphism, and has the additive parameter law.
hypotheses: The stated Zorn basis; any commutative unital ring, including characteristics two and three.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.g2_short_root_preserves_quadratic; Sage g2_forms.py complete norm polynomial, 343 tensor triples, 64 octonion products and additive parameter law over Z[t,s].
limitations: This verifies the explicit one-parameter operator, not construction or classification of the full G2 group scheme.

claim: Listed natural A/B/C/G2 modules have chain diagrams; dual modules retain the chain shape.
hypotheses: Must specify equivalence up to duality and low-rank coincidences, and nontrivial irreducible highest-weight modules.
verification: checks/sage/classical_diagrams.py confirms listed shapes; duality sends every weight to its negative, preserving root-difference edge labels.
limitations: Global classification of all irreducible chain weight diagrams is no longer asserted.

claim: The E₆ minuscule weight orbit has 27 weights of multiplicity one, dual highest weight ω₆, and diagram W(E₆)/W(D₅).
hypotheses: Highest weight omega1; Bourbaki numbering.
verification: checks/sage/weight_diagrams.py and checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py generate the full Weyl orbit and all 36 labelled edges; the roots fixing ω₁ form D₅.
limitations: Independent finite root data, not proof of module freeness over every ring.

claim: Every E6 root action has six disjoint linear coordinate pairs; example alpha1+alpha3+alpha4 matches highlighted diagram.
hypotheses: 27-dimensional minuscule module; root parameter arbitrary, signs from fixed integral basis.
verification: checks/sage/e6_representation.py all 72 root matrices preserve cubic; checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies six pairs and marked graph action. weight_diagrams.py counts six coordinate pairs for every root and eight paths but six pairs for alpha1+alpha3+alpha4.
limitations: Endpoint-pair counts do not prescribe signs along arbitrary paths. Distinct paths with the same endpoints do not give additional coordinate actions.

claim: F=detx+dety+detz−tr(xyz) defines split E6 cubic, and its polynomial isometry scheme is Gsc(E6).
hypotheses: Mat3(Z)^3 and arbitrary base change; polynomial rather than pointwise equality on finite rings.
verification: Conrad2015 formula6.6 and TheoremC.2, LemmasC.3–C.4/proof read; Vavilov1996 §8p93 verifies minus convention.
limitations: Comparison of weight-basis cubic with Mat3 model not explicitly constructed here; see separate weight-form bridge entry.

claim: Nondegenerate homogeneous form degree≥3 has finite linear isometry group in characteristic zero.
hypotheses: Meaning of nondegenerate (smooth projective hypersurface) and degree/dimension exceptions must be specified.
verification: Orlik1978 is cited, but the exact nondegeneracy definition and theorem exceptions have not been verified.
limitations: The broad finiteness assertion is unresolved without its precise hypotheses.

claim: Given semisimple group has tensor stabilizer; irreducible tensor-indecomposable groups maximal subject to exceptions.
hypotheses: Fixed algebraically closed field; characteristic and explicitly listed exceptions.
verification: Dynkin, Seitz and Testerman are cited; the complete exception list and applicable theorem hypotheses have not been verified.
limitations: Irreducibility alone does not establish maximality of a tensor stabilizer.

claim: Split eight-dimensional composition algebra is unique with zero divisors; canonical involution/trace; Hermitian model has Jordan product.
hypotheses: Field characteristic≠2,3; gamma_i units; split octonions.
verification: Conrad2015, Appendix B, supplies the split composition model. The Jordan identity, uniqueness and twisted Hermitian construction need a separately checked source theorem.
limitations: Jordan identity/uniqueness and gamma-twisted Hermitian algebra not tested or independently proved here.

claim: Hermitian gamma-dependent entries, determinant cubic, quadratic trace form and Freudenthal cross product normalization.
hypotheses: Field characteristic≠2,3; gamma_i units; f(x,x,x)=detx.
verification: The Hermitian entry conditions follow by comparing entries in g⁻¹(a*)ᵗg=a. The determinant, trace and cross-product normalization require a verified Faulkner1977 locator.
limitations: No complete polynomial verification of the nonassociative determinant or Jordan/cross-product relation is recorded.

claim: The 27-dimensional Jordan diagram splits into three scalar components and three eight-dimensional components.
hypotheses: Restricted D4 graph with edges1,6 removed.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the three singleton and three eight-node restricted Weyl orbits.
limitations: Checks weight-space partition, not full Jordan multiplication.

claim: A5+A1 decomposition V=U⊕Λ²U*⊕U, equivalently U⊕Λ⁴U⊕U; natural pairing determines cubic.
hypotheses: U natural rank 6, chosen determinant trivialization.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies component sizes 6, 15 and 6. The perfect exterior pairing gives Λ⁴U≅Λ²U* after choosing a determinant trivialization; the complete equivariant cubic construction is not verified.
limitations: Dimension/component agreement does not certify equivariant tensor/cubic construction.

claim: Schlafli root-difference graph has diameter 2, degree 16, ten non-neighbours; D5 vector/half-spin subsets.
hypotheses: 27 E6 minuscule weights.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies all 27 weights, graph degree 16, diameter two, common-neighbour counts 10 and 8, and restricted D₅ orbits of sizes 10 and 16.
limitations: Distance-transitivity not directly asserted by the script; separate entry.

claim: The Schläfli graph is distance-transitive; a nonadjacent pair has a unique third weight completing a cubic triple.
hypotheses: Full E6 Weyl action on minuscule orbit.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the cubic incidences. Transitivity of the restricted W(D₅) orbits of sizes 16 and 10 gives distance-transitivity.
limitations: Incidence symmetry does not by itself prove invariance of the coefficient signs.

claim: There are 45 unordered cubic triples and 270 ordered triples; the proposed ordered-triple stabilizer has type D₄.
hypotheses: Triple consists pairwise nonadjacent distinct weights.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the 45 triples; six orderings give 270. The complete faithful stabilizer identification is not independently verified.
limitations: Counts alone do not certify the full Weyl-group stabilizer.

claim: 45 cubic triples identify with tritangent planes of cubic surface.
hypotheses: Classical complex/algebraically closed smooth cubic-surface identification.
verification: Coxeter1963 is cited; a complete geometric correspondence between root incidences and cubic-surface lines has not been verified.
limitations: Root incidence checks alone do not verify algebraic-geometric line correspondence.

claim: The signed 45-term weight cubic is invariant under the integral root operators; its invariant line is unique over Q.
hypotheses: Specified integral Chevalley basis; distinguished sign+1.
verification: checks/sage/e6_representation.py verifies all 72 root actions over Z[t], generator relations and the one-dimensional invariant kernel over Q. checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py checks torus exponents and cubic support.
limitations: Rational invariant uniqueness alone does not identify an integral stabilizer. The separate checks/sage/e6_norm_model.py certificate supplies the integral norm-model isometry.

claim: The signed weight-basis cubic is asserted to have split simply connected E₆ as its stabilizer after every base change.
hypotheses: Polynomial equality after arbitrary base change.
verification: checks/sage/e6_norm_model.py verifies the complete identity N(Su)=f(u) over Z and det(S)=1 for the signed-permutation matrix S. Its integral inverse conjugates the two polynomial isometry functors after every commutative base change. Conrad2015, formula (6.6) and Theorem C.2, with Lemmas C.3–C.4, identifies the norm-model stabilizer.
limitations: The integral change of basis and polynomial identity are computationally certified; smoothness, connectedness and the group-scheme identification are supplied by the independently read primary-source theorem, not proved by Sage.

claim: Root torus multiplies six weights by epsilon, six by epsilon^-1; weight torus exponents1,−1,0 with multiplicities1,10,16; cubic is relative invariant.
hypotheses: Chosen torus/weight-element normalization.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the torus exponents, their multiplicities and the corresponding exponent sum on each cubic triple.
limitations: Scheme identification of extended group requires separate source theorem.

claim: Complete polarization has diagonal 6F; the integral quadratic and cubic refinements retain the information lost by division by two or six.
hypotheses: Square-free cubic support; every commutative ring.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the universal monomial identities; summing the 45 square-free monomials proves the displayed polarization and cross-product relations.
limitations: Division by two or six is not permitted in small characteristic.

claim: The integral Mat₃ norm stabilizer is the split E₆ group scheme.
hypotheses: Integral polynomial stabilizer.
verification: Conrad2015, Lemmas C.3–C.4 and the proof of Theorem C.2, establish flatness, connectedness and the required root structure.
limitations: A primary-source scheme proof, not a numerical tangent-space test or a Lean theorem.

claim: White, grey and black vectors have the stated geometric rank/orbit classification; the black E₆ orbit depends on its nonzero norm.
hypotheses: Algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two and three; the extended group is used for a single black orbit.
verification: Mars1966 is cited, but a complete verified orbit-theorem locator is not recorded.
limitations: The restriction to algebraically closed fields does not by itself verify the classification.

claim: A cubic isometry has a white first column; the proposed reduction yields blocks of sizes 1, 16 and 10.
hypotheses: Algebraically closed characteristic≠2,3; geometric orbit theorem required.
verification: The highest-weight vector has zero quadratic adjoint; cubic isometries preserve that locus. The verified cubic incidences yield the hyperbolic pairing on the ten-weight component.
limitations: Transitivity and simultaneous row/column reduction remain unverified; the orthogonal block alone does not identify the full stabilizer.

claim: The extended E₆ model is described by norm similarities; polarization is equivalent when six is invertible.
hypotheses: Unit multiplier; polynomial identities after arbitrary base change.
verification: The polarization equivalence follows by coefficient comparison. The full extended-group identification needs a precise independently checked similarity-scheme theorem.
limitations: The E₆ isometry theorem alone does not identify the full similarity scheme.

claim: The split F₄ group is described as the automorphism group of the split Albert algebra and an identity stabilizer inside E₆.
hypotheses: The field and characteristic hypotheses of the Jordan model must be specified.
verification: Chevalley1950 and Jacobson are cited; a complete applicable identification theorem is not verified here.
limitations: No universal-ring or characteristic-two scheme identification is certified.

claim: The restricted F₄ module has 24 nonzero weights and a three-dimensional zero-weight space, including the fixed identity line.
hypotheses: Restriction of the E₆ module; omitted zero-space action is outside the diagram coverage.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the minimal character with 24 nonzero weights and zero multiplicity two, plus the fixed line, and all visible labelled edges.
limitations: The action on the zero-weight space is not fully drawn or checked by the diagram comparison.

claim: The stated F₄ root matrices have the specified off-diagonal entry counts and ranks.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero; nonzero parameter; the chosen basis.
verification: No complete signed F₄ generator matrix calculation or verified primary-source locator is recorded.
limitations: Weight multiplicities do not certify basis-dependent matrix-entry counts or ranks.

claim: The E₇ minuscule module has 56 weights, a perfect alternating form and root operators of rank 12; its E₆ grading has sizes 1, 27, 27 and 1.
hypotheses: Split integral Chevalley model; a nonzero parameter for nonzero-entry counts.
verification: checks/sage/e7_invariant.py checks the independent Sage weight orbit, all 126 root operators, square-zero and symplectic identities, and the generator relations. checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the diagram.
limitations: The weight grading is not a semisimple branching theorem in every characteristic.

claim: The alternating-matrix model has dimension 56 and the stated Pfaffian/trace quartic is invariant under the E₇ root operators.
hypotheses: Characteristic zero for the displayed fractional formulas; six invertible for polarization equivalence.
verification: checks/sage/e7_invariant.py verifies the full 56-variable quartic over Q[t], coefficient ratio (1,1,−1/4,1/16), symplectic preservation and generator relations.
limitations: Root invariance does not prove that the entire stabilizer equals E₇; no integral extension is inferred from the fractional formula.

claim: An integral nonsymmetric four-linear form and alternating form define simply connected E₇; the extended scheme stabilizes the ideal of 133 quadrics.
hypotheses: Every commutative ring by base change from Z.
verification: VavilovLuzgarev2016, Theorems 1–2, constructions §§3–4 and proof §9, pp. 19–20 of the English author manuscript.
limitations: The source is a later work of the original author and a coauthor. The complete integral form, fibre and scheme arguments have not been independently reproduced. The rational quartic root-invariance check does not supply them.

claim: The Brown and exterior-power descriptions have dimensions 1+27+27+1 and 7+21+21+7, with the stated characteristic-two qualifications.
hypotheses: Fields satisfying the hypotheses of the particular tensor construction.
verification: Dimensions follow from the exterior powers and the Jordan rank 27. Complete Brown/Aschbacher tensor identities and the coefficient-two calculation are not verified.
limitations: No explicit ternary-product implementation or verified characteristic-two theorem locator is recorded.

claim: The E₈ adjoint weight grading has dimension 248, with E₇ pieces of sizes 1, 56, 133, 56, 1 and 1.
hypotheses: Integral weight grading; semisimplicity in every characteristic is not asserted.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the independent root sets and counts: 57 positive roots outside E₇, 27 outside E₆, and 36 positive E₆ roots; the negative and Cartan parts give dimensions 248 and 133.
limitations: Root counts verify the grading. The separate assertion that the adjoint module is the smallest E₈ representation requires a highest-weight classification.

claim: The three displayed adjoint fragments have the correct vertices, labelled simple-root edges and exits.
hypotheses: Displayed positive-root portions; omitted Cartan-action links are excluded.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py compares complete independent Sage root sets and edge lists and rejects duplicates.
limitations: No complete adjoint-action matrix diagram is claimed.

claim: The normalized integral E₈ pairing is unimodular, the Killing form is 60B, and the displayed bracket-derived tensors are invariant.
hypotheses: Integral Chevalley basis with opposite-root pairing one; arbitrary base change.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the 240 root contributions to the Killing trace and determinant one of the 248-dimensional Gram matrix. Invariance and bracket antisymmetry give the tensor identities.
limitations: The script verifies Gram and trace data, not all bracket coefficients; the invariant Chevalley-pairing identities are algebraic inputs.

claim: Single tensor stabilizers admit unwanted scalar symmetries; the pair (B,f) reconstructs the bracket, and the Killing form vanishes in characteristics two, three and five.
hypotheses: Perfect B; scalar multiplier ζ with ζ³=1 or ζ⁴=1 for the respective tensor.
verification: checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py verifies the scalar obstructions. Multilinearity supplies degrees three and four; Killing=60B explains the characteristics. Perfectness represents f(x,y,−) by a unique bracket vector.
limitations: The common stabilizer is identified with B-preserving Lie-algebra automorphisms, not automatically with E₈ over every ring.

claim: Absolute and relative elementary normality and the standard commutator inclusions; equality under the stated small-residue-field exclusions.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; irreducible root system of rank at least two. Equality excludes B2/G2 with an F2 residue field.
verification: Taddei1985/Taddei1986 normality; Vaserstein1986b Theorem 3, full source read for the relative commutator assertions.
limitations: No extension to rank one or to arbitrary noncommutative coefficient rings. Mixed two-ideal formula has additional hypotheses.

claim: Elementary-normalised subgroups have a unique ideal sandwich.
hypotheses: Rank at least two; 2 invertible for B/C/F4; for G2, 3 invertible and no F2 residue field; commutative unital ring.
verification: Vaserstein1986b Theorems 3–4, full proof and hypotheses read.
limitations: Not a Lean proof; without invertibility restrictions levels can depend on root length.

claim: Root extraction in all quotient rings, together with the standard commutator formula, yields the ideal sandwich.
hypotheses: The standard-normal-structure restrictions; relative normality; root-level generation and relative perfectness over every quotient.
verification: Vaserstein1986b Theorems 3–4; explicit quotient argument in the text: the root and all elementary conjugates become central modulo F∩E, so relative perfectness forces their normal closure into F.
limitations: Parabolic extraction is a separate theorem, not a consequence of a Levi decomposition. No arbitrary nonsplit-kernel intersection equality is used.

claim: Rank-one behaviour differs from higher-rank normality and classification.
hypotheses: Rank-one groups and the particular rings indicated in the historical discussion.
verification: Historical primary references cited in the section; no new universal rank-one theorem asserted.
limitations: Examples are not a classification of all rank-one groups over all rings.

claim: Factoring by a two-sided ideal in the Jacobson radical preserves standard normal structure of GL(n,R).
hypotheses: Associative unital ring; n≥3; J contained in the Jacobson radical.
verification: Stepanov1999 §4 Theorem 4.6 and proof, Corollary 4.7, author preprint p9, full text and separate erratum read.
limitations: Does not settle the exact class of rings or the separate conjecture about normal subgroups inside E(n,R).

claim: Rank-one square-zero operators give invertible transvections with inverse obtained by negating the parameter.
hypotheses: Finite free module over a commutative unital ring; vu=0. The square-zero inverse identity itself allows any associative unital ring.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.rank_one_square_zero and Vavilov1991.square_zero_unipotent_inverse.
limitations: Determinant, root type and elementary membership are not formalized by these declarations.

claim: 1+YX has inverse 1−YZX when Z is a two-sided inverse of 1+XY.
hypotheses: Arbitrary finite rectangular dimensions over an associative unital ring; specified inverse Z.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.rectangular_jacobson_right and Vavilov1991.rectangular_jacobson_left; also jacobson_inverse_right/left.
limitations: No assertion concerning ideals or elementary groups follows solely from the inverse calculation.

claim: The four unipotent block factors equal diag(1+XY,1−YZX).
hypotheses: Associative unital ring; finite rectangular blocks; Z two-sided inverse of 1+XY.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.whitehead_four_factors; checks/sage/whitehead.py.
limitations: Sage alone covers only its selected 2×3/3×2 dimensions.

claim: The five-factor form lies in the relative elementary group when Y has entries in the ideal.
hypotheses: Associative unital ring, two-sided ideal I, finite positive block sizes, entries of Y in I, Z inverse of 1+XY.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.whitehead_five_factors and whitehead_relative_parameter; textual factor-membership proof; Suslin1977 §1 Lemma 1.1, Quillen1995 p174 read.
limitations: Lean does not formalize elementary-group membership. The original missing inverse was corrected.

claim: A rank-one transvection with one zero row or column coordinate is relative elementary.
hypotheses: Associative unital ring and two-sided ideal; coefficient order as printed; vu=0 and vj=0, or the row counterpart.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.zero_coordinate_commutator, zero_component_factorization, transvection_entries_in_ideal; explicit normal-closure membership argument.
limitations: The elementary group itself and the transposed counterpart are not formalized.

claim: Stable row reduction gives GL(n,R)=GL(n−1,R)E(n,R), hence relative elementary normality.
hypotheses: Stable-rank condition n≥sr(R)+1; rows and right coefficients in the stated order; associative unital ring.
verification: Bass1964/Bass1967 stable-range result; Vaserstein1981 Lemma 9 p458, full paper read; direct multiplication of the displayed row operations.
limitations: Stable-row-reduction signs are not formalized in Lean. This route does not remove the stable-rank bound.

claim: Every u orthogonal to a unimodular row v has the exact triangular Koszul decomposition displayed.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; finite linearly ordered index set; vw=1 and vu=0.
verification: Lean Vavilov1991.suslin_component, koszulRelation_syzygy, suslin_decomposition, suslin_triangular_decomposition.
limitations: The subsequent elementary normality proof is an argument using the separate zero-component lemma, not this Lean theorem alone.

claim: The syzygy decomposition and zero-component lemma prove relative elementary normality.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring, n≥3, ideal I; conjugated rows unimodular.
verification: Suslin1977 §1 and the explicit argument in the text; Lean-decomposed syzygies and zero-component identities as separate inputs.
limitations: No full group-normality theorem has been formalized in Lean.

claim: Column-stabilising factors multiply to the desired elementary root element and their conjugates are relative elementary.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring, n≥3, invertible g, ξ in I; auxiliary distinct index3.
verification: Direct inverse-matrix sums and multiplication; zero-component commutator lemma; unimodular centre has explicit left inverse f1 g−1.
limitations: No inference from fixing a column alone: unimodularity is essential to obtain the zero row coordinate. This complete group argument is not formalized.

claim: A noncentral elementary-normalised linear subgroup has a noncentral element preserving a coordinate line.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; n≥3; g noncentral; subgroup normalised by E.
verification: Borevich1985 proof and independently checked rank-one commutators, antisymmetry and unit ideal of 2×2 minors of two rows of an invertible matrix.
limitations: Does not by itself prove the parabolic extraction theorem. No Lean formalization of the minors argument.

claim: A polynomial matrix equal to identity at zero is elementary iff all maximal localisations are elementary.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring, n≥3, g(0)=1.
verification: Suslin1976 local-global theorem; Stepanov2014 §§2.4–2.6, full dissertation read.
limitations: Not a consequence of injectivity into a localisation; arbitrary elements may be zero divisors. No Lean implementation of patching.

claim: ESD transformations and their conjugation preserve the orthogonal form.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring, 2 invertible, isotropic mutually orthogonal defining vectors; nondegenerate stated form.
verification: Hahn1989b §§5.1C,5.2D,5.3D read; direct rank-two formula; checks/sage/orthogonal_transvections.py.
limitations: The Sage rational model does not establish arbitrary-ring elementary membership.

claim: The three commuting root factors have the displayed six-dimensional matrix and fixed-column syzygies.
hypotheses: Three mutually orthogonal isotropic directions; parameters as printed; common scalar permitted.
verification: checks/sage/orthogonal_transvections.py and checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py.
limitations: No assertion that every product is a single ESD transvection. No elementary membership from a fixed vector alone.

claim: The orthogonal column-stabilising factors multiply to T_(1,−2)(ξ).
hypotheses: Split orthogonal model and invertible form-preserving g; commutative ring; ESD coordinate formula uses 2 invertible.
verification: Displayed inverse-matrix contractions, commutativity of the three root groups; checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py verifies fixed-column polynomial identities.
limitations: Not a proof of elementary membership of their conjugates; this step is explicitly separated.

claim: Split orthogonal elementary groups are absolutely and relatively normal.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; irreducible B/D rank at least two; no stable-rank or invertibility-of-two requirement for the uniform theorem.
verification: Taddei1985/Taddei1986; complete split-pullback proof at passage:relative-normality-pullback.
limitations: A parabolic can have nontrivial Levi K1. No unsupported fixed-column⇒elementary implication is used.

claim: The isotropic elementary group is independent of a strictly proper parabolic and normal.
hypotheses: After localisation at every maximal ideal, every relative irreducible component has rank at least two; strictly proper means meeting every nontrivial semisimple normal component properly.
verification: PetrovStavrova2009 Theorem 1, full source read.
limitations: A single split torus of rank two is insufficient. Form-ideal settings may require more than one ideal; no universal nonsplit normal-structure classification is inferred.

claim: The corrected tilde convention, long/short rank-one formulas, form preservation and conjugation.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; alternating nondegenerate F; for short transformations (u,v)=0; division by two only where 2 is invertible.
verification: Direct expansion using F transpose=−F and isotropy; checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py and checks/sage/classical_forms.py.
limitations: No claim of arbitrary-vector elementary membership.

claim: Long/short product equals T_(ηu+θv)(1) and the coordinate choice fixes a column.
hypotheses: Orthogonal u,v; commutative ring; displayed rank-two Witt coordinates.
verification: checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py; direct vanishing of all cross terms.
limitations: Summing squares does not reconstruct a prescribed root parameter; the text explicitly records this limitation.

claim: Signed minors solve the two fixed-column linear equations.
hypotheses: Any commutative ring; any two columns; no division; common multiplier permitted.
verification: checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py; determinant expansion with repeated columns.
limitations: They solve the associated linear factor, not all subsequent parabolic/elementary membership questions.

claim: The corrected central parameter and the two displayed factors reproduce the short-root product.
hypotheses: Commutative ring; displayed product parameter2θ−ζη; convenient short-root parametrisation assumes 2 invertible.
verification: checks/sage/stabiliser_identities.py.
limitations: The subsequent higher-rank Cauchy–Binet/parabolic discussion is an outline; it is not a completed independent elementary-membership proof.

claim: Absolute and relative symplectic elementary normality hold without invertibility of two; the mixed formula requires separate hypotheses.
hypotheses: C_l rank≥2; commutative unital ring. HVZ mixed theorem additionally excludes F2 residues in C2 and requires c∈c²R+2cR in type C.
verification: Taddei1985/Taddei1986; split-pullback argument; HazratVavilovZhang2013 Theorem 1 full source read.
limitations: Mixed formula is not a normal-subgroup classification. No full Lean Chevalley theorem.

claim: Freudenthal transformation preserves the cubic for orthogonal white column and white row, and the displayed basis case equals x_(α1).
hypotheses: Integral27-dimensional model; vu=0; both u and v white; opposite column/dual cross-product signs.
verification: Vavilov2000 §4.2 full text read; checks/sage/e6_representation.py checks all 702 ordered distinct basis pairs and the complete simple-root matrix. Vavilov2000 is a later work of the original author, not an independent source.
limitations: The both-white preservation theorem is supported by a later work of the original author, not an independent source. The 702 basis-pair checks certify the root-operator cases, not arbitrary white vectors.

claim: The five listed roots form a singular commuting family with root differences.
hypotheses: E6 Bourbaki-order conversion specified; chosen integral Chevalley basis.
verification: checks/sage/e6_representation.py and checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py; independently generated E6 root system and pairwise root/operator tests.
limitations: No unverified identification of signs with the faded original diagram.

claim: The signed five-root product fixes every white column.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; parameters sρξuρ with s=(1,1,1,1,−1); vanishing gradient of the integral cubic.
verification: checks/sage/e6_representation.py integral27-dimensional matrices and invariant cubic; checks/sage/exceptional_weights.py diagram labels.
limitations: Whiteness is required; does not prove general group-scheme identification or elementary membership.

claim: The column-factor argument proves absolute E6 elementary normality using the elementary parabolic lemma for fake-root unipotents.
hypotheses: Commutative unital ring; split simply connected minimal E6 model; fake-root shape A_m; Weyl-conjugate P1.
verification: Vavilov2000 §4.3 Proposition 2, full published statement and context read; inverse-matrix summation and preceding verified white-column identities. Vavilov2000 is a later work of the original author, not an independent source.
limitations: The fake-root parabolic-membership lemma is taken from a later work of the original author; its full independent verification is not recorded. The factor and column calculations are checked. No general parabolic-to-elementary implication is asserted.

claim: Absolute normality over all coefficient rings implies relative normality using the split double ring.
hypotheses: Chevalley group over commutative unital R; ideal I; absolute elementary normality over every commutative coefficient ring; R′={(a,b):a−b∈I}, J′={(a,0):a∈I}.
verification: Vaserstein1986b §2 p221 read; complete root-word splitting and diagonal-section proof in the text.
limitations: Does not assert E(R)∩G(R,I)=E(R,I) for an arbitrary nonsplit quotient. No Lean formalization of group functors.

claim: For D_(n−1)⊂D_n, n≥4, overgroups have unique levels given by submodules of R² and elementary/stabiliser bounds.
hypotheses: Every commutative unital ring; this particular subsystem and n≥4.
verification: Gvozdevsky2022 Theorem 1 and §11.1, full arXiv2107.01258v2 statement, definitions, proof reduction and special case read.
limitations: Not a solution for arbitrary subsystem, subring or homomorphism; no normality of the lower bound in the upper stabiliser asserted.

claim: Standard normal structure holds for the specified isotropic reductive groups.
hypotheses: Every semisimple normal R-subgroup contains Gm²; absolute root systems in all geometric closed fibres irreducible; structure constants invertible.
verification: Stavrova2024 Theorem 1.1, full arXiv1801.08748v2 definitions and main proof §§7–10 read.
limitations: No extension to isotropic rank one, reducible absolute fibres or noninvertible bad structure constants.

claim: Finite-rank constructions suggest research directions for infinite-dimensional groups.
hypotheses: No universal infinite-dimensional root-system or ring hypothesis specified.
verification: Read as an explicitly qualified research direction, not a mathematical theorem.
limitations: No general infinite-dimensional normality or classification claimed.

claim: One white argument alone does not ensure preservation of the E₆ cubic.
hypotheses: The corrected integral cross-product signs; u=e₀, v=e₁*+e₁₄*, with vu=0 and u white.
verification: checks/sage/e6_representation.py verifies a nonzero integer-polynomial cubic difference and an integral test vector whose cubic changes from 13 to 1.
limitations: A counterexample to the stronger hypothesis; not a proof of the general both-white preservation theorem.

claim: The universal inverse-matrix algebra of size m>1 has E(m,R) neither normal nor subnormal in GL(m,R).
hypotheses: Any field K; two generic noncommuting m-by-m matrices subject to xy=yx=1; m>1 and the same matrix size in the group.
verification: Gerasimov1989 §10, printed pp. 61–62, full primary text read; specialize its universal representation construction to the infinite cyclic group.
limitations: Primary-source verification only; the free-product theorem and non-subnormality are not formalized in Lean.
